newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr strengthens on EMU jitters, bourses mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr strengthens on EMU jitters, bourses mixed.

text.p: The dollar climbed against the mark in early trade on Monday as jitters over the European single currency resurfaced but European bourses, preoccupied by domestic issues, opened in a mixed mood.

London dipped slightly in cautious dealings ahead of Wednesday's budget, expected to contain bad news for investors. Frankfurt and Paris flitted in and out of profit in lacklustre morning business. The main action was in currency markets, where fresh uncertainty over European economic and monetary union (EMU) drove the dollar up by almost a pfennig to 1.7458 marks. Sterling was also at 59-months highs against the German currency.

Investors moved into safe haven currencies after a rift within German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling alliance over EMU widened at the weekend with one of his partners raising the prospect of leaving the coalition.
The row pits members of Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) against its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), and above all Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber.

Stoiber is calling for a delay in monetary union if the entry criteria are weakened. He has threatened to block German membership of EMU in the upper house of parliament unless the criteria are strictly met.
"Uncertainty over European monetary union is supporting the dollar and sterling," Nick Shamin, currency analyst at ANZ Investment, said.
"The talk (in Germany) about the euro can only help support the dollar...We should see a test of the top side again," said Peter Wood, trader at Bank of Boston.
Sterling rose after stronger-than-expected British data and hovered at 2.8923 marks, just below near-six year highs of 2.8945 set overnight.

The U.S. currency was also given a lift by figures on Monday showing French unemployment rose 1.1 per cent in May. Traders said rising unemployment raised the spectre of a delay to EMU or a soft euro from the outset.

In equity markets, London opened higher but quickly turned negative with investors pulling in their horns ahead of the new Labour government's budget amid talk that it could hit dividend tax breaks for pension funds.
Fears were also growing that interest rates would be increased to quell the current strength of consumer demand.
"There had been so much speculation about the budget and I can't see the major funds wanting to do anything for the next couple of days," said one dealer.
The market is likely to be edgy this week ahead of a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's monetary policy-makers, analysts said.
Few expect an immediate U.S. interest rate rise but the central bank is likely to be alert for any signs that the underlying strength of the economy could feed inflation in coming months.
Frankfurt made modest gains, underpinned by the stronger dollar, which helps exporters, and Friday's Wall Street gains. The blue-chip DAX index was up 0.25 percent by mid-morning.
Paris shed its opening profits and was down 8.51 points at 2,882.53 in early trading on the CAC-40 index.
Car-maker Renault fell 1.16 percent at 153.70 francs on profit-taking. Brokers say the closure of the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium, confirmed over the weekend, was priced into the share.
In thin trading on bullion markets, gold was fixed at $334.05 an ounce, its lowest price for 4-1/2 years, under pressure from the strong dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 114.55 yen and 1.7458 marks, compared with 114.62 and 1.7365 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 7.1 points at 4,633.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 slipped 8.51 points to 2,882.53.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 10.40 points at 3,805.81.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $334.05 an ounce against $337.15 at Friday's close. Silver was at $4.72, down two cents.
